Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we prepare our internal procurement packet, we need a written explanation of two things so we can take to finance/legal: 1) how a marginal ladder differs from a blended effective rate in practice (examples please), and 2) whether Redwood will consider an "anchored" commit (small baseline commit with larger marginal step-downs) vs a straight blended-floor proposal.

Our internal forecast is attached (Zektronics_2028_forecast.xlsx) — we expect to start at ~200M tokens/month for Q1, ramping toward ~2B tokens/month over 9–12 months if latency and accuracy hold.

Key asks: clear examples (numbers) showing the same usage under both approaches, and a recommended structure you think balances our need to cap unit cost early while allowing Redwood to protect throughput economics.

Can you send a write-up this week? We'll aim to get legal engaged next week.

Subject: RE: Clarification on per-token ladder + forecast attached

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the forecast — helpful context. We're preparing a short write-up with concrete math and one practical proposal that tends to work well for customers in a ramp: an "anchored hybrid" that pairs a modest committed baseline (blended floor) with marginal breakpoints above that baseline.

High-level:
- Baseline commit (blended): protects you from rate volatility on the first chunk of tokens and gives Redwood predictability.
- Marginal ladder above baseline: as you cross breakpoints, each additional token is billed at the step rate (not retroactively). This keeps incentives aligned and typically drives a lower marginal price at scale.

I'm looping Ben (finance) and Soojin (contracts) — they'll confirm guardrails (true-ups, clawbacks) and suggest a draft we can send to procurement. Expect a detailed example in a few hours.

— Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: INTERNAL: Zektronics pricing math — hybrid anchored example

Team —

Emma asked for a concrete comparison (marginal ladder vs blended effective). Below is a working draft of numbers to validate with finance/legal before we share externally. Please sanity-check and punch the numbers into a quick simulation.

Assumptions (example month):
- Usage scenario: 750M tokens in a single month (mid-ramp)
- Proposed breakpoints (above baseline): 10M, 100M, 1B
- Step marginal rates (per-token):
  * 0–10M: baseline blended floor = $0.00012 (applies to baseline commit only)
  * 10M–100M: marginal $0.000085
  * 100M–1B: marginal $0.00006
  * >1B: marginal $0.000045

Hybrid anchored approach (example structure):
- Commit: 100M tokens/month (12-month term) billed at blended floor of $0.00012 (commit covers first 100M)
- Above commit: billed on marginal ladder above (tokens beyond 100M billed per step)

Sample math for 750M usage in month (quick calc):
- Baseline 100M at $0.00012 = $12,000
- Next  (10M–100M) 90M at $0.000085 = $7,650
- Next  (100M–750M => 650M at $0.00006) = $39,000
- Total = $58,650 effective per-token = $58,650 / 750,000,000 = $0.0000782

Compare to a pure blended offer (single effective rate for all tokens) we might quote to get same revenue for Redwood: effective blended ~$0.00008–$0.00009 depending on commitment term/credits.

Questions for legal/finance:
- Do we allow retrospective re-rating (no) — marginal steps apply to tokens at time of consumption only.
- True-up: monthly on actual usage with quarterly review for smoothing.
- Shortfall/underutilization: propose credits to roll into next quarter (cap at 25% of committed value) or pre-paid commit offsets.

Ben — can you run this through a 12-month ramp (use Emma's attached forecast) and attach a CSV with effective blended math?
Soojin — can you flag any contract language we should pre-seed (clawback, minimum ramp covenant, termination for convenience with penalty)?
Laura — if we move forward, I want a concise external one-pager showing both the blended equivalent and the marginal example.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa / team —

Quick pass attached (ZEK_rate_simulation.csv). A few notes:
- Under Emma's 12-month ramp, effective blended for months 1–3 is ~ $0.000105; months 4–9 drop toward $0.00007 as they hit higher breakpoints.
- Recommend adding a mild "anchor protection" clause: if actual trailing 90-day usage is < 50% of forecast, Redwood can shift to a minimum blended floor for the following quarter (simple language — protects capacity planning).
- For procurement friendliness, add an optional "convert to blended" clause at month 6 if both parties agree (helps legal signoff).

If you want, I can generate a second simulation where we cap total monthly overage discounts (to protect against sudden burst exploitation).

Subject: Zektronics pricing proposal (hybrid anchored per-token model)

Hi Emma —

Appended below is a concise proposal and two worked examples (marginal ladder vs blended equivalent) based on the forecast you sent. Attached is a formal PDF we can send to procurement (20280110-zektronics-proposal.pdf).

Proposal (high level):
- Term: 12 months with quarterly true-ups
- Commit: 100M tokens/month at blended baseline $0.00012 (committed monthly credit)
- Above commit: marginal ladder applies to incremental tokens
  * 0–10M above baseline: $0.000085
  * 10M–900M above baseline: $0.00006
  * >1B above baseline: $0.000045
- Underutilization: unused committed value may be converted to credits up to 25% per quarter or rolled forward once (one-time roll).
- Anchor protection: if trailing 90-day usage drops below 50% of forecast, Redwood may request a temporary re-rate to blended floor for the next quarter (this protects long-term capacity planning).
- Optional conversion: at month 6 both parties may elect to convert to a single blended rate for simplicity (subject to mutual agreement).

Worked example (month with 750M total usage):
- Commit 100M @ $0.00012 = $12,000
- Next 90M @ $0.000085 = $7,650
- Next 560M @ $0.00006 = $33,600
- Remaining 0 (since 100+90+560=750)
- Total = $53,250 => effective per-token = $53,250 / 750,000,000 = $0.000071

Pure blended illustrative quote to yield similar Redwood revenue: ~$0.000075–$0.00008 (would be a flat per-token price across all usage for the month). The hybrid tends to give you cheaper marginal cost as you ramp while protecting Redwood on the baseline.

Next steps:
1) If this matches your expectations, we'll produce an SOW and redline-friendly term sheet for procurement/GC.
2) I can open a DocuSign SOW (we've added a draft link below) or we can schedule a one-hour pricing review with our finance and contracts team this week.

Attachments: 20280110-zektronics-proposal.pdf (proposal + simple table), ZEK_rate_simulation.csv (internal sim)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DEAL-98765

Thanks —
Marissa
